messages:
Sara Patel: ran a 1h perf sweep against the new dev fleet with real traffic replay. surprising: host-side CPU dominates for short requests (<=64 tokens). tokenization + parse + http2/gRPC framing ~65-75% of host cpu on p50.
Mike R: can you paste the numbers?
Sara Patel: p50 total latency 12ms, gpu decode 4ms, host overhead 6.5ms, syscalls+writev 1.2ms, tokenization ~2.8ms, parse+proto 1.5ms, http2 encode 0.9ms.
Leo G: that aligns with kvcache traces i pulled — hot shard thrash adds ~300-500µs when many concurrent short seqs hit same key.
Alice Chen: hmm. two vectors: reduce tokenization cost (pretokenize/shim at edge or cached tokenized prefixes) and reduce tiny-request overhead (coalesce http writes / smallwrite batching).
Sara Patel: I experimented with pretokenizing in the proxy (edge sidecar). when request has header `x-rtokenize: cached`, parse stage bypasses tokenizer and we see host drop from 6.5ms -> 3.9ms for those requests.
Mike R: nice. is pretokenize safe re: model vocab changes?
Sara Patel: need pinning + model-version header. we only enable when request model == pinned tokenizer version. fallback to regular path otherwise.
Leo G: for kvcache: i saw eviction storms when prefix popularity changes. suggestion: add jittered TTL and per-shard admission > threshold so hot key doesn't thrash eviction.
Alice Chen: agree. also kernel selection tweak: for seq_len <= 64 pick kernel A (fast small-seq path), for 65-256 pick kernel B, else kernel C. current runtime picks B for everything which regresses small seq throughput. pseudocode: `if seq<=64 -> KERNEL_SMALL; elif seq<=256 -> KERNEL_MED; else -> KERNEL_LONG`
Mike R: can we detect tokenized input and skip further parse allocations? maybe mark buffer as `TOKENIZED` and set parser to `fast-path` – small patch:
```// parser.go
if req.Flags&FLAG_TOKENIZED != 0 {
  buf = req.Payload // avoid Tokenize(buf)
  goto fast_path
}
```
Alice Chen: +1. also we should coalesce streaming chunks: for grpc streaming small frames, increase max-accumulate-time to 1-2ms to allow bundling multiple small writes into one writev. tradeoff: adds tiny tail for some requests but reduces syscall pressure.
Sara Patel: benchmark: enabling 2ms coalesce reduced syscalls by 40% and host CPU by ~0.8ms p50.
Leo G: don't forget backpressure: bundling must respect client-level latency SLO. maybe adaptive: if queue length OR util > X then coalesce, else immediate flush.
Mike R: can we do an A/B canary? infra-bot: deploy plan started for channel=eng-runtime , target=canary-7, change=pretokenize + small-kernel-selection + grpc-coalesce, run=2h.
Sara Patel: posting perf run logs to the exec board after canary. will include flamegraphs and syscall traces.
Alice Chen: follow-ups: (1) make kernel selector rule config, (2) implement tokenized flag path in parser, (3) grpc coalesce adaptive threshold, (4) kvcache jittered-ttl patch. assign owners?
Mike R: I'll take (2) and help with tests.
Leo G: i'll do (4) + telemetry for hot-shard alerts.
Sara Patel: i'll own (1) + run canary and collect metrics.
Alice Chen: thanks. if no blockers i'll file PRs and tag reviewers. :thumbsup:
